title: Repository structure and version control
caption: The recreated repository keeps the original layered layout: application, migrations, tests, container build, CI pipeline, Kubernetes manifests, infrastructure code, monitoring and logging. The Git history at the top shows the imported baseline commit.

title: Python runtime and dependency verification
caption: A clean virtual environment installs every pinned runtime and development package and pip check reports no broken requirements. Versions are pinned so the container image and a developer workstation resolve exactly the same dependency set.

title: Automated test suite
caption: Parametrised unit tests cover validation rules, release metadata, error handling and security headers. The same suite runs inside the test stage of the container image and is invoked by the Jenkins pipeline through scripts/test.sh, together with the PostgreSQL integration tests.

title: Application service startup and health endpoints
caption: Gunicorn serves the single-worker runtime image on port 8090. Liveness answers immediately, the release endpoint reports the application name and semantic version, and the HTML dashboard is served with the hardening headers. Readiness returns 503 on this build host because no PostgreSQL instance is present, which is exactly the behaviour the Kubernetes readiness probe relies on.

title: Prometheus metrics endpoint
caption: The application publishes request, response, latency and error counters plus a database availability gauge in Prometheus text format. Prometheus scrapes this endpoint for both the Compose and the Kubernetes deployments, and Grafana renders the resulting series.

title: Registered API and probe routes
caption: Every route is registered under the taskflow blueprint with explicit HTTP methods. The same route names appear as normalised metric labels, so cardinality stays bounded and no task identifier leaks into the metrics.

title: Multi-stage container build definition
caption: The Dockerfile builds a shared base layer, a test target that adds pytest and the test suite, and a hardened runtime target that runs as UID 10001 with a health check. Jenkins builds the runtime target while scripts/test.sh builds the test target.

title: Local Compose stack
caption: The Compose stack wires the application to PostgreSQL on separate frontend and internal database networks, publishes the interface on loopback, and applies read-only root filesystems, dropped capabilities and no-new-privileges to the runtime container.

title: Continuous integration pipeline stages
caption: The declarative Jenkinsfile defines seven stages. Tests must pass before an image is built, Bandit and pip-audit run on the source, Trivy records HIGH and CRITICAL findings, and the final stage commits the new image tag back to the manifest so Argo CD can deliver it.

title: Jenkins test, scan and build stages
caption: Excerpt of the pipeline definition: the isolated test runner, Bandit with severity and confidence thresholds, pip-audit against the pinned runtime requirements, and a Docker build that embeds the version, commit SHA and build date as OCI labels.

title: Kubernetes resource inventory
caption: Nine objects across seven manifest files, all valid and namespaced: configuration, the database bootstrap SQL, the application Deployment and Service, a NodePort used for monitoring, the PostgreSQL Service and StatefulSet, the Green release, and the Argo CD Application.

title: Application Deployment with rolling update
caption: Two replicas run behind a ClusterIP Service with maxUnavailable 0. The pod runs as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem, a memory-backed /tmp volume, startup, readiness and liveness probes, and CPU and memory requests and limits.

title: PostgreSQL StatefulSet and persistent storage
caption: The database runs as a single-replica StatefulSet behind a headless Service with a 2 GiB volume claim. The bootstrap ConfigMap creates the application role and schema once, on a fresh volume, and every credential is read from a Secret rather than committed to Git.

title: Terraform cluster provisioning
caption: Terraform manages the dedicated Minikube profile used by the whole capstone. The resource is replace-triggered on profile, CPU or memory changes and destroys the cluster on terraform destroy, so the infrastructure is reproducible instead of hand-built.

title: Ansible namespace and quota configuration
caption: The playbook verifies the dedicated cluster context, waits for nodes to become Ready, then applies the development and production namespaces with their resource quotas and limit ranges. The tasks report changed only when kubectl actually creates or updates something, so a second run is idempotent.

title: Argo CD GitOps application
caption: Argo CD watches the kubernetes directory on the main branch of this repository, syncs it into taskflow-prod with self-healing enabled and pruning disabled, so a manual incident response action is never silently reverted.

title: Prometheus scrape configuration
caption: Prometheus scrapes the Compose application through host.docker.internal and the Kubernetes NodePort Service, and Grafana is provisioned alongside it in the same Compose project.

title: Logstash pipeline for centralised logging
caption: Application JSON logs are forwarded from Kubernetes over TCP, parsed as JSON lines and indexed into Elasticsearch under a daily taskflow-logs index that Kibana discovers.

title: Blue-green release strategy
caption: Blue and Green Deployments run side by side with different image tags. The production Service selector is the only thing that changes, which makes both the release and the rollback a single Git commit that Argo CD reconciles.

title: End-to-end DevOps architecture
caption: Three layers with clear ownership: automation and source control, a gated build that produces one immutable artefact, and GitOps delivery into Kubernetes with the observability stack alongside it.

title: Continuous integration and GitOps delivery flow
caption: Ordered, gated stages replace manual releases. Because the manifest update is itself a commit, every deployment has an audit trail and can be rolled back with git revert.

title: TaskFlow application dashboard
caption: The Flask dashboard served by the Compose stack: five synthetic sample tasks, live status counts, status filters and a backend health indicator. Task content is rendered as text and the interface is served with a strict content security policy.

title: Static validation of manifests, scripts and modules
caption: All fourteen YAML files and twenty-one documents parse cleanly, every Python module byte-compiles and both shell scripts pass bash -n. This is the same validation Jenkins performs implicitly when it builds and applies the manifests.
